correctness.rationale: The included verify_dodecahedron.py (standard library) was executed and passed all exact ring checks. The proof reduces all generic central cuts to sign-crossing edges of the 20-vertex 30-edge dodecahedron. Ten antipodal vertex axes yield 45 circle pairs, 90 distinct oriented intersections, with exact nonconcurrency. Each local four-sector sign vector is exhaustively generated; all 92 sign chambers are grouped by (section sides, chamber corners, angle-cosine multiset) as (6,6,20), (8,3,60), (10,5,12). Every sign decision is an integer comparison in Z[sqrt(5)]. Girard spherical excess gives areas 2π−3(α+β), 2α+β−π, 2π−5α and they sum to 4π with weights. The independent expectation from thirty edge crossings equals 30β/π and agrees exactly. Genericity exceptions are 10 great circles and Haar null.

Same 10-circle chamber combinatorics are old; the mathematical claim being assessed is the full mapping from each chamber family to planar dodecahedron section sidedness and exact Haar probability law, neither displayed nor implied without this nontrivial dodecahedral edge-incidence analysis in inspected sources. The closest icosahedron law is not dual-equivalent: polar duality takes sections to projections. value.rationale: An exact complete distribution for a natural, symmetry-distinguished random geometric section of the 20-vertex Platonic solid, distinguishing three section types of strictly positive Haar probability. Beyond the known arrangement face counts, the 92-cell edge-incidence classification identifies which chamber orbits correspond to the geometric section observables; the probabilities and independent first moment have closed elementary formulas. The computational finite table has a structural object motivation (random central stereology of a regular dodecahedron) and is exhaustive by the sign-chamber argument; it is neither a parameter substitution in the icosahedron case nor an arbitrary slice. Earlier published great-circle area fractions are not relabeled as discoveries.
